From fe6653460ee7a7dbe0cd5fd322992af862ce5ab0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pan Bian <bianpan2016@163.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2021 01:18:47 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] mtd: spi-nor: hisi-sfc: Put child node np on error path

Put the child node np when it fails to get or register device.

Fixes: e523f11141bd ("mtd: spi-nor: add hisilicon spi-nor flash controller driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Pan Bian <bianpan2016@163.com>
[ta: Add Fixes tag and Cc stable]
Signed-off-by: Tudor Ambarus <tudor.ambarus@microchip.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210121091847.85362-1-bianpan2016@163.com

diff --git a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
index 7c26f8f565cb..47fbf1d1e557 100644
--- a/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
+++ b/drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c
@@ -399,8 +399,10 @@ static int hisi_spi_nor_register_all(struct hifmc_host *host)
 
 	for_each_available_child_of_node(dev->of_node, np) {
 		ret = hisi_spi_nor_register(np, host);
-		if (ret)
+		if (ret) {
+			of_node_put(np);
 			goto fail;
+		}
 
 		if (host->num_chip == HIFMC_MAX_CHIP_NUM) {
 			dev_warn(dev, "Flash device number exceeds the maximum chipselect number\n");
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/mtd/spi-nor/controllers/hisi-sfc.c`**
- A new line was added to the error handling section of the `hisi_spi_nor_register_all` function. Specifically, when the `hisi_spi_nor_register(np, host)` call fails (i.e., `ret` is non-zero), the child node `np` is now released using `of_node_put(np)` before the function exits with a `goto fail` statement. This ensures that the reference to the child node is properly decremented, preventing potential memory leaks.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug related to resource management in the `hisi-sfc` driver. By adding the `of_node_put(np)` call, the patch ensures that the child node is correctly released when an error occurs during device registration. This change is directly related to the previous commit identified by the Fixes tag, which introduced the `hisi-sfc` driver. The patch improves the robustness of the driver by ensuring proper cleanup in error scenarios.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
ret = hisi_spi_nor_register(np, host);
if (ret)
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because if the `hisi_spi_nor_register` function fails (indicated by a non-zero `ret`), the reference to the child node (`np`) is not decremented. This results in a memory leak since the allocated node remains in memory without being released.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
of_node_put(np);
```
Reason:
The patch adds a call to `of_node_put(np);` in the error handling path. This ensures that when the registration fails, the reference to the child node is properly decremented, preventing the memory leak by releasing the allocated node.
